_doc: Four named scale tiers, each pre-answered with concrete numbers so a feature spec or PRD can DECLARE a tier instead of being interrogated about scale nobody stated. `_default` is what `plan_feature.py new` / `prd.py new` apply when `--scale` is omitted. `required` is what that tier's design must do; `not_required` is the more valuable half -- it is what licenses an agent to keep things simple, and is what research/00-signal-rubric.md Part G (rule 4, 'scale-appropriate') and skills/approach-selection/SKILL.md ('do not choose for a requirement nobody stated') were missing a mechanism for. Latency-budget REASONING is owned by skills/performance-budgets/SKILL.md; this file supplies only the default p95 number each tier starts from -- it does not repeat that skill's rules.
_alignment: These four map onto research/35-findings-security-reliability.md's 'security baseline by scale' synthesis so the plugin has ONE scale vocabulary, not two: prototype ~ its 'solo / hobby project with external users', small ~ its 'small team (2-10)', growth ~ its 'org (10+, multiple maintainers, sustained external adoption)', scale ~ its 'high-blast-radius (CNCF-tier infrastructure ... or anything a large number of downstream systems build on)'. Consult that synthesis for the security-specific half of each tier; this file covers capacity, latency, and architecture.

prototype.label: Prototype
prototype.users_requests: < 100 total users (or pre-launch/internal only); < 1 req/s sustained, bursts don't matter
prototype.instances: single instance, no replica, no failover
prototype.availability_target: best-effort, no SLA -- downtime during iteration is expected and acceptable
prototype.p95_note: deliberately generous: correctness over speed. A number is still stated (performance-budgets rule 1 requires one), it just isn't a tight one.
required: input validation at the boundary
one documented rollback step per change
a single, honestly-scoped pre-commit verification command
not_required: deliberate connection-pool sizing beyond the framework default
rate-limiting infrastructure beyond a basic per-account counter
sources: research/35-findings-security-reliability.md synthesis, 'Solo / hobby project with external users' (one documented pre-commit command, commit crash inputs as they happen)
scripts/data/decisions_required.json 'search' kind default ('database full-text first; a dedicated index only once a measured limit is hit') -- applies a fortiori below that limit
SOURCE: original for the p95 number itself

small.label: Small
small.users_requests: < 10,000 users; low tens of requests/sec at peak
small.data_volume: up to low millions of rows per table / tens of GB total
small.instances: one primary instance (plus an optional standby); vertical scaling (a bigger box) is an acceptable answer to growth
small.availability_target: single-region uptime; manual or semi-automated failover is fine, not automatic
small.p95_note: the worked save-action budget in reviewers/_latency-numbers.md (browser -> gateway -> app -> DB, one or two same-DC round trips) -- realistic without any exotic infra.
required: indexes on the query paths actually used; EXPLAIN before merging a new query against a non-trivial table
bounded/paginated list queries (unbounded pagination is a correctness bug at any size, not a growth-tier nicety)
a deliberately sized connection pool, not the driver default
a stated p95 budget split across hops
basic uptime/error-rate monitoring
not_required: a dedicated cache layer (Redis/Memcached) unless a measured hot path needs it
sources: reviewers/_latency-numbers.md 'A worked budget example' (300ms p95 save action) and its HikariCP connection-pool-sizing citation (brettwooldridge/HikariCP.wiki:About-Pool-Sizing.md)
skills/performance-budgets/SKILL.md rules 1, 5, 6, 7, 'Scale' section (solo tier: rules 4/6/8/9 free/near-free; small-team adds 3, 5)

growth.label: Growth
growth.users_requests: < 1,000,000 users; hundreds to low thousands of requests/sec at peak
growth.data_volume: up to roughly 100M+ rows in a hot table; write-heavy paths need explicit index-cost discipline
growth.instances: multiple instances behind a load balancer; HA and automatic failover expected
growth.availability_target: automatic failover within one region; a numeric target (e.g. 99.9%) stated and tracked
growth.p95_note: tighter than 'small' because a multi-instance, multi-dependency call chain has more places for tail latency to hide (performance-budgets rule 2: reason in p95/p99, never the mean).
required: multi-instance deployment with HA/failover
a cache with a stated hit-rate assumption AND a stated answer for 0% hit rate (cold start / post-deploy)
capacity headroom: name which resource saturates first as load grows 10x
load, soak, and spike testing before a capacity-relevant release
rate limiting at the gateway
cost-per-request tracked next to latency in any capacity review
not_required: per-query cost accounting on every single query in the system
a dedicated security team with a rotating fix lead
sharding or partitioning -- read replicas are enough until a measured ceiling is actually hit
sources: skills/performance-budgets/SKILL.md rules 11, 12, 14, 15 and 'Scale' section ('org / high-blast-radius: add 7, 11, 12, 14, 15, 16')
research/35-findings-security-reliability.md synthesis, 'Org (10+, multiple maintainers, sustained external adoption)'

kubernetes/community@master:sig-scalability/configs-and-limits/thresholds.md -- illustrates the discipline this tier adopts: explicit numeric ceilings per resource (e.g. 3000 pods/namespace, 250 endpoints/service), not adjectives

scale.label: Scale
scale.users_requests: > 1,000,000 users, OR any regulated / high-blast-radius data regardless of user count
scale.data_volume: unbounded by design; partitioning/sharding planned before a table hits its measured ceiling, not after
scale.instances: multi-region, multiple instances per region, automated failover across regions
scale.availability_target: a numeric SLO with an error budget (e.g. 99.95%+), tracked and alerted on by percentile
scale.p95_note: same-region target; a cross-region hop adds ~150ms WAN RTT on top (reviewers/_latency-numbers.md, colin-scott/interactive_latencies) and must be budgeted for explicitly wherever a request crosses regions.
required: multi-region topology, budgeted explicitly around cross-region RTT
every new query/endpoint costed: rows scanned and $/request tracked, not just latency
capacity planning against a stated numeric threshold, not an adjective -- the way kubernetes' own scalability-thresholds doc states hard numbers per resource
an explicit availability target/SLO with an error budget
a documented sharding/partitioning strategy
the org / high-blast-radius security baseline in full (research/35-findings-security-reliability.md synthesis)
not_required: adopting a larger company's practice with no failure class named for it -- cargo-culting is rejected at every tier, this one included (research/00-signal-rubric.md Part G rule 1)
rewriting a boring, working component because a checklist mentions a fancier option
an exotic consistency model nobody's workload actually requires
sources: research/35-findings-security-reliability.md synthesis, 'High-blast-radius (CNCF-tier infrastructure, browser/OS-adjacent, or anything a large number of downstream systems build on)'

kubernetes/community@master:sig-scalability/configs-and-limits/thresholds.md (numeric per-resource thresholds, e.g. 5000 nodes/cluster, 150000 pods/cluster -- the pattern this tier imitates: a number, not a vibe)
